paths.description: Homepage schedule/listing template and primary discovery entry point; tested desktop, 360px mobile, dark, high contrast, reduced motion, no-JS, performance, network, security, accessibility and memory.
Representative live-match detail and watch journey; tested desktop/mobile, player state, injected overlays, metadata and runtime dependencies. Represents duplicate match pages.
Representative editorial article template selected from sitemap; tested content semantics, metadata, imagery, desktop and mobile reflow. Represents duplicate article pages.
Deliberately nonexistent route to evaluate HTTP/network failure handling and recovery.

findings.summary: The site remains light-only when the user requests a dark color scheme.
findings.evidence: The dark-mode screenshot is pixel-identical in appearance and byte size (52,600 bytes) to the default screenshot; the CSS probe found no color-scheme or prefers-color-scheme support.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme: light dark and use prefers-color-scheme or light-dark() for page, card, text, and control colors.

findings.summary: Long-list navigation is abrupt and provides no scroll-aware orientation or transition cue.
findings.evidence: The CSS/DOM probe found no View Transition, scroll timeline, anchor-positioning, or container-query rules; the page is 7,098px tall and its header remains static.
findings.suggestedFix: Add progressive cross-document View Transitions and a lightweight scroll-state cue or progress affordance for the long schedule.

findings.summary: A transparent advertising layer is injected directly over the live player, obstructing and deceiving the primary watch action.
findings.evidence: Rendered DOM shows aclib.runPop(zoneId 8630206), a hidden adexchangerapid link, and an injected transparent absolute-positioned 690x430 div over the 690x430 player. The player also loads ad scripts over HTTP. The before/after programmatic video click screenshots remain unchanged.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove the pop-under/transparent click-capture advertising integration. Make the player itself the direct, keyboard-operable primary action and expose honest playback/error state.

findings.summary: Missing URLs do not present a truthful error or recovery state.
findings.evidence: A deliberately nonexistent route returned 302 and silently landed on the homepage with no 404 message; failed player guidance only says to refresh.
findings.suggestedFix: Return an actual 404 status and a clear not-found page with home/search links; give player failures explicit status, retry, and alternate-channel controls.

findings.summary: Mobile loading performance misses the modern LCP bar and ships a heavy initial page.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured LCP 9,684.8ms and performance score 0.57. HAR recorded 48 requests and 3,256,843 transferred bytes, including 2,322,820 image bytes.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritise the actual LCP asset, remove nonessential third parties from initial load, lazy-load below-fold media, and reduce image/font payloads.

findings.summary: Images are unreserved, oversized, legacy-format, and eagerly loaded far below the fold.
findings.evidence: The image audit found 49/49 missing width/height, 47 oversized, 47 below-fold images without lazy loading, and 39 legacy-format images. HAR attributes 2.32MB to images.
findings.suggestedFix: Set intrinsic width/height, serve correctly sized AVIF/WebP responsive sources, and lazy-load below-fold images while prioritising only the LCP image.

findings.summary: The accessibility tree and interaction targets contain widespread naming, contrast, hierarchy, and sizing failures.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse accessibility score was 0.74 with failures for color contrast, link names, target size, frame title and accessibility tree. The DOM probe counted 214 empty-text links among 343 links, headings begin at H3 before H1, and Lighthouse reported 37 undersized/overlapping target groups.
findings.suggestedFix: Repair link markup so each card is one named target, use logical H1/H2 hierarchy and landmarks, meet WCAG contrast, and provide at least 24x24 CSS-pixel targets with adequate spacing.

findings.summary: Malformed repetitive anchor markup and incorrect image presentation undermine document and asset quality.
findings.evidence: Rendered DOM contains nested/unclosed anchors that wrap large parts of the document. Lighthouse failed image-aspect-ratio, while the image audit found every image missing intrinsic dimensions.
findings.suggestedFix: Validate and repair HTML nesting, use one semantic anchor per card/action, and set accurate intrinsic image dimensions/aspect ratios.

findings.summary: The page triggers browser inspector/BFCache hygiene failures and relies on stale third-party script patterns.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse best-practices score was 0.52 and failed inspector-issues and BFCache audits. Rendered match DOM loads multiple ad scripts and latest unpinned Clappr at runtime.
findings.suggestedFix: Resolve DevTools inspector issues, remove unload/BFCache blockers, pin and update dependencies, and eliminate obsolete ad-loader scripts.

findings.summary: Article and match pages lack page-specific indexing and sharing metadata.
findings.evidence: The article uses generic title “FawaNews - Your Home of Sport”, has no H1, Open Graph tags, or JSON-LD. The match page has no canonical in the probe. /robots.txt returns homepage HTML and Lighthouse robots audit scored 0.
findings.suggestedFix: Give every page a unique title/description/H1 and canonical, add accurate Article/VideoObject JSON-LD and Open Graph tags, and serve valid robots.txt plus a current sitemap.

findings.summary: The site is served over insecure HTTP with no browser security headers and insecure cookies.
findings.evidence: Headers audit reports HTTPS false and all six checked defenses absent: CSP, HSTS, nosniff, clickjacking protection, Referrer-Policy and Permissions-Policy. All 9 cookies lack Secure and use SameSite=None; HTTPS probing failed certificate hostname validation for www.fawanews.sc.
findings.suggestedFix: Serve all pages/resources through valid HTTPS, redirect HTTP, then deploy HSTS, CSP with frame-ancestors, nosniff, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy, and Secure/Lax cookies.

findings.summary: The page has a disproportionate and opaque third-party tracking/ad footprint.
findings.evidence: Tracker audit found 11 third-party origins including Google Tag Manager, Google Analytics and Histats. HAR recorded 37 third-party requests and 2,532,744 third-party bytes; match pages add pop-ad, X and CDN scripts.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove pop-ad/Histats integrations, audit every remaining third party, obtain meaningful consent where required, and defer/batch minimal analytics.

findings.summary: The live-view runtime depends on fragile mixed-origin scripts and provides no robust failure state.
findings.evidence: The player source is an HTTP IP-address HLS URL and the page injects HTTP ad scripts. The only recovery instruction is “If Lags, Refresh The Page”; a missing URL is silently redirected.
findings.suggestedFix: Use HTTPS media and first-party controlled dependencies, detect media/network failures, and expose explicit retry/channel/error states without page reload.

findings.summary: Global sports pages are not consistently language- or locale-ready.
findings.evidence: The match document has no html lang, the CSS probe counted 695 physical left/right properties and no dir attribute, and schedules are hard-coded as GMT+1 despite an international audience.
findings.suggestedFix: Set lang and dir on every template, migrate layout to logical properties, store times unambiguously, and render schedule times with Intl for the viewer locale/time zone.

findings.summary: Resource use is far above what a text/listing page needs, dominated by avoidable third-party imagery and fonts.
findings.evidence: HAR transferred 3.26MB, including 2.32MB images and 506.8KB fonts; 2.53MB came from third parties. Image audit found 47 oversized images and 39 legacy formats.
findings.suggestedFix: Adopt an explicit page-weight budget, replace repeated remote avatars with small cached responsive modern-format assets, subset fonts, and defer nonessential embeds.

taskList.title: Remove transparent/pop-under ad capture from the player and make playback honest and directly operable
Move the entire site and media path to valid HTTPS with defensive headers and secure cookies
Cut initial payload by optimising/lazy-loading images and removing nonessential trackers
Repair semantic card/link/heading markup, contrast, focus, and target sizing
Add truthful 404 and media/network error recovery states
Add page-specific canonical, title, H1, Open Graph, JSON-LD, robots.txt, and sitemap signals
Add dark-mode support and locale/time-zone-aware rendering
